constraints: New private workspace package packages/agent-tools (@exharness/agent-tools, type module, node >=20) with no runtime npm dependencies; it imports Core from ../../core-harness/src/index.js and the BB-096 adapters from ../../agentic-system/src/index.js, the same relative convention packages/agentic-system uses.

Every process is started with spawn and an argument array and shell:false; on win32 an npm .cmd/.ps1 shim is resolved to its JavaScript entry and run with process.execPath, and cmd.exe/powershell are never used.

Every test in the package is titled with its criterion prefix (AT1..AT4 followed by a space), declares { timeout: 60000 }, uses only fake CLIs and temp git repositories, and removes worktrees and temp dirs in finally blocks.

Root package.json gains test:agent-tools (node --test packages/agent-tools/test/*.test.js) appended to the test script, and smoke:agent-tools (node packages/agent-tools/bin/exharness-agent.mjs smoke) which is not part of test or verify.
Adapters are not a sandbox; docs must state that live runs execute with the user's CLI permissions inside a temp worktree only and point isolation to BB-067.
Research only in this lane: no product source edits, no self-issued readiness or fabricated Jev judgment.
invariants: Only a candidate whose declared verifications all PASS at its exact commit can be promoted; the agent exit status or message never contributes to acceptance.
Agent processes run only in an isolated worktree under os.tmpdir(); the source repository HEAD, branches and working tree are never modified.
No process is started through a shell, and every agent invocation is bounded by a timeout that kills its process tree.
User CLI configuration and credentials are never read or written by the adapters.
architectureDecisions: D1 — Files: packages/agent-tools/{package.json, src/index.js, src/tool-adapters.js, src/process-runner.js, src/supervisor.js, bin/exharness-agent.mjs, test/agent-tools.test.js, test/fixtures/fake-agent.mjs}. Root exports: defineAgentTool, codexTool, kiroTool, agyTool, runAgentInvocation, createSupervisedAgentStrategy, runSupervisedTask, AgentTaskStatus.

D2 — AGENT_TOOL_ADAPTER_V1 = { id, command, prefixArgs = [], versionArgs, buildInvocation({ prompt, resume, model, permissionProfile, logFile, timeoutMs }) -> { args, stdin } where resume is null for a first invocation or { sessionRef } (sessionRef may be null) for a resume, parseResult({ exitCode, stdout, stderr }) -> { claimedSuccess, finalMessage, sessionRef } }. defineAgentTool(base, { command, prefixArgs }) overrides only the executable so tests can substitute a fake while keeping the real argument builder.

D3 — Invocations. Flags and values present in the executed probe help output: codex exec --json/--sandbox workspace-write|danger-full-access/--skip-git-repo-check/--model, codex exec resume [SESSION_ID] [PROMPT] with `-` reading the prompt from stdin, plus --json; kiro-cli chat --no-interactive/--trust-tools=<list> (help example fs_read,fs_write)/--trust-all-tools/--resume/--model; agy --print/--continue/--mode accept-edits/--dangerously-skip-permissions/--log-file/--print-timeout/--model. codex first = [exec, --json, --skip-git-repo-check, --sandbox, workspace-write (FULL_AUTO: danger-full-access), (--model m), -] with the prompt on stdin; resume = [exec, resume, <resume.sessionRef>, --json, -] with the prompt on stdin, where sessionRef is the thread_id/session_id that codex parseResult extracted from the --json stream of the first invocation; when resume.sessionRef is null the codex adapter builds a fresh first invocation instead. kiro and agy ignore sessionRef because their resume is scoped to the worktree cwd. kiro first = [chat, --no-interactive, --trust-tools=fs_read,fs_write,execute_bash (FULL_AUTO: --trust-all-tools), (--model m), <prompt>]; resume inserts --resume after chat. agy first = [--print, <prompt>, --mode, accept-edits (FULL_AUTO: --dangerously-skip-permissions instead of --mode), --print-timeout, <timeoutSeconds>s, (--model m), --log-file, <path>]; resume inserts --continue. The process cwd is always the worktree root. The installed Kiro binary contains the built-in tool name execute_bash; agy help prints the --print-timeout default as 5m0s, so timeoutSeconds is a positive integer rounded up from timeoutMs and formatted as a Go-style seconds duration. Worker re-runs the probe for version drift before implementation.

D4 — runAgentInvocation(tool, request, { cwd, env = {}, timeoutMs = 600000, maxOutputBytes = 1048576 }) spawns tool.command with [...prefixArgs, ...args] and process.env overlaid with env, writes stdin when present, streams stdout/stderr through incremental SHA-256 digests while retaining at most maxOutputBytes per stream (recording truncation), and on timeout kills the process tree (POSIX: detached + process.kill(-pid, "SIGKILL"); win32: spawn taskkill with ["/pid", String(pid), "/T", "/F"] and shell:false, then wait for both taskkill and the tool to exit). It returns { exitCode, signal, timedOut, durationMs, stdout, stderr, stdoutSha256, stderrSha256, truncated }. A missing executable (ENOENT) returns { status: "TOOL_UNAVAILABLE", exitCode: null, timedOut: false } without throwing. The supervisor applies tool.parseResult to normal exit results; it never treats parsed claimedSuccess as verification. resolveExecutable(command, { platform, pathEnv }) searches PATH; on win32, when the hit is an npm shim (<name>.cmd or <name>.ps1 next to node_modules), it returns { command: process.execPath, prefixArgs: [<absolute JS entry parsed from the shim target>] }; native .exe hits are returned unchanged. An explicit absolute .mjs/.js --command path, including the fake CLI fixture, resolves to { command: process.execPath, prefixArgs: [that path] }; this resolution precedes PATH lookup.

D5 — Supervisor: runSupervisedTask({ tool, task, model = null, maxAttempts = 3, timeoutMs, maxFeedbackChars = 8000, permissionProfile, env = {}, eventSinks = [], tracer = null }) creates a unique worktreeRoot under os.tmpdir(), creates a BB-096 createLocalGitWorkspace({ repositoryRoot: task.repositoryRoot, baseRevision: task.baseRevision, worktreeRoot }), then probes tool.versionArgs from that worktree with a bounded shell-free invocation to set toolVersion and one BB-096 createLocalCommandVerifier per task.verifications entry (claim = `agent-task.${name}`, requireUnchangedTree true). It composes createHarness({ strategy: createSupervisedAgentStrategy(...), environment: workspace, verifiers, verificationPolicy: { requirements: one { claim } per declared verifier }, variationPolicy: { maxCapabilityCalls: maxAttempts * (verifiers.length + 3) }, objective, eventSinks, tracer }), calls harness.start({ work: { id: task.id, prompt: task.prompt }, seedCandidate: { id: task.id, version: task.baseRevision } }), retains the returned sessionId, and runs exactly one harness.vary(sessionId) whose strategy performs all attempts (Core allows several ACT/EVALUATE calls in one variation and PROMOTE only after a PASS evaluation of the current candidate). The workspace is disposed in finally.

D6 — Attempt loop inside strategy.run({ input, invoke }): attempt 1 prompt = task.prompt; attempt n>1 prompt = task.prompt + a bounded feedback block whose first line is exactly `ExHarness verification failed:` followed by each failing verifier name, status, reason and output tail (total <= maxFeedbackChars), invoked with resume. After each invocation: if HEAD moved, `git reset --soft <candidate.version>` and record AGENT_COMMITS_FOLDED; edits = every added/modified file path from `git status --porcelain -z --untracked-files=all` with its current content read from the worktree; invoke AVOCapability.ACT with { kind: "APPLY_BACKEND_CHANGE", edits } (the action kind BB-096 act accepts; it commits and stages deletions via git add -A); invoke verificationCapabilityName(name) for each declared verifier; invoke EVALUATE; only a PASS on a mutated candidate invokes PROMOTE and returns ACCEPTED. A non-mutating ACT is recorded as NO_CHANGE and counts as an attempt even if the base revision passes verification; Core forbids promoting the unchanged lineage head. After maxAttempts return EXHAUSTED.

D7 — objective.evaluate returns PASS only when Core-supplied verifications for the current candidate contain a PASS record for every declared verifier; tool claimedSuccess/finalMessage are stored in the attempt record only.

D8 — AGENT_TASK_V1 = { id, repositoryRoot, baseRevision (40-hex), prompt, verifications: non-empty [{ name, command, args, timeoutMs }] } validated before any process starts; verifier names are unique, commands are non-empty strings, args are string arrays, and timeoutMs values are positive integers. AGENT_SUPERVISED_RESULT_V1 = { taskId, tool, toolVersion, status ACCEPTED|EXHAUSTED|TOOL_UNAVAILABLE, attempts: [{ index, resume, exitCode, timedOut, durationMs, claimedSuccess, candidateSha, mutated, foldedAgentCommits, verification: [{ name, status, reason }], feedbackChars }], acceptedSha }.

D9 — bin/exharness-agent.mjs: `run --tool <codex|kiro|agy> --task <task.json> [--command <path>] [--max-attempts N] [--timeout-ms T] [--permission WORKSPACE_EDIT|FULL_AUTO]` prints AGENT_SUPERVISED_RESULT_V1; `probe` prints versions; `smoke --tool <t> [--command <path>]` creates a temp repo with one failing test and a one-line fix prompt, runs the supervised loop and prints the result, or prints SKIPPED with reason NOT_INSTALLED (executable missing) or TOOL_FAILED_BEFORE_EDIT (tool exited non-zero with no change on attempt 1, which is how a missing login or credential surfaces); --command selects the executable while retaining the tool argument builder; a .mjs/.js path is launched through process.execPath as in D4 (used by tests); it never reports ACCEPTED without a passing verification.

D10 — Fake CLI fixture test/fixtures/fake-agent.mjs selects behavior from env FAKE_AGENT_SCENARIO: FIX_FIRST, FIX_AFTER_FEEDBACK (fixes only when its prompt contains the line `ExHarness verification failed:`), NEVER_FIX, CLAIM_SUCCESS_NO_EDIT, SELF_COMMIT, AUTH_FAIL (exit non-zero without edits), HANG. It records its pid, spawned child pid for HANG, argv and stdin to a JSON file for assertions; HANG spawns a long-lived child so AT2 can verify tree termination. It answers versionArgs with `fake-agent <FAKE_AGENT_VERSION or 0.0.0>`, implements "fix" as `git apply <FAKE_AGENT_SOLUTION_PATCH>` in its cwd when that env var is set and otherwise writes the built-in fix of the AT3 fixture, and when invoked with codex-style argv emits a first JSONL line {"type":"thread.started","thread_id":"fake-<n>"}.

D11 — Evidence basis: executed probe shows all three CLIs installed with non-interactive, resume and permission flags; only codex has --json; no ExHarness code launches external agents; BB-066 names only OpenHands.
implementationSlices: S1 — Adapters + fake CLI [AT1]: implement D2-D3 and the D10 fake CLI fixture first, because every later slice tests against it. "AT1 ..." tests assert exact argv and stdin per tool and profile including agy timeout formatting for resume null, resume { sessionRef: "s-1" } and resume { sessionRef: null }, that codex parseResult extracts sessionRef from a thread.started line, that a prompt containing `; & | " $()` reaches the fake verbatim, that a missing executable yields TOOL_UNAVAILABLE, and that resolveExecutable with platform win32 over a synthetic PATH directory containing a fake npm shim or explicit .mjs path returns process.execPath plus the JS entry while a native .exe is returned unchanged. Files: packages/agent-tools/package.json, src/index.js, src/tool-adapters.js, test/fixtures/fake-agent.mjs, test/agent-tools.test.js. Verified by at1-adapters.

S2 — Process runner [AT2]: implement D4. "AT2 ..." tests cover exit code capture, output truncation flag and full-stream digests despite bounded retained text, and HANG with timeoutMs 500 returning timedOut within 10s with both the recorded parent and child pids no longer alive (process.kill(pid, 0) fails for each). Files: src/process-runner.js. Verified by at2-runner.

S3 — Supervisor [AT3]: implement D5-D8. "AT3 ..." tests on temp git repos cover FIX_FIRST -> ACCEPTED in 1 attempt; FIX_AFTER_FEEDBACK -> ACCEPTED in 2 attempts with resume argv and feedback text observed by the fake; NEVER_FIX -> EXHAUSTED after maxAttempts with no PROMOTE; CLAIM_SUCCESS_NO_EDIT -> not ACCEPTED with NO_CHANGE; a separate already-passing seed case also cannot PROMOTE without a mutated candidate; SELF_COMMIT -> folded into one candidate; source repository unchanged in every case (HEAD, `git branch --list` and `git status --porcelain` compared before/after). The four main scenarios use a temp repo whose test/app.test.js fails until src/app.js returns 42, with task.verifications = [{ name: "tests", command: process.execPath, args: ["--test", "test/"] }]. Files: src/supervisor.js. Verified by at3-supervisor.

S4 — CLI + smoke + docs [AT4]: implement D9. "AT4 ..." tests run the bin `run` against the fake tool (task.json plus a --command override to the fake) and parse the result, and `smoke --tool codex --command <nonexistent path>` yields SKIPPED NOT_INSTALLED and smoke with the AUTH_FAIL fake yields SKIPPED TOOL_FAILED_BEFORE_EDIT; neither prints ACCEPTED. Add root scripts, write docs/living/system/agent-tools/state.md and link it from docs/living/system/state.md, then run test:agent-tools, verify:current-docs and npm test. Files: bin/exharness-agent.mjs, package.json, docs/living/system/agent-tools/state.md, docs/living/system/state.md. Verified by at4-cli, agent-tools, docs and repository.

dependencyResolution.contradiction: Unresolved upstream source-protection conflict: the task invariant requires the source repository HEAD, branches and working tree never to change, while the plan excludes sandbox isolation and permits FULL_AUTO agent commands. A temp worktree and cwd do not confine an agent process; its .git file points back to source git metadata. Exact readiness requires either an upstream narrowing of the guarantee to harness-controlled operations or adding an isolation dependency with enforceable filesystem boundaries. If a D3 flag is absent at the installed tool version, or BB-096 act cannot commit agent-made worktree changes without editing packages/agentic-system, stop PLAN_INPUT_CONTRADICTION.

objectiveCoverage.objectiveCriterion: Specify tool adapters for Codex, Kiro and agy that build exact shell-free non-interactive and resume invocations with explicit permission profiles, resolve Windows npm shims without cmd.exe, and report an unavailable tool as TOOL_UNAVAILABLE.
Specify one bounded process runner that captures bounded output with digests, redacts nothing it does not own, and terminates the whole process tree on timeout.

Specify an ExHarness-supervised loop on Core createHarness and the BB-096 workspace/verifiers where each agent invocation is an ACT candidate, only passing declared verification can PROMOTE, failures feed back through tool resume up to maxAttempts, agent commits are folded into one candidate and the agent claim is telemetry only.
Specify a CLI entrypoint and an opt-in live smoke that never fakes success when a tool is missing or unauthenticated, plus Living docs stating the no-sandbox trust boundary.
Ground the design in the executed agent CLI probe and produce an exact file-level plan, fake-CLI fixtures, negative cases and executable verification for fresh Jev readiness.

negativeVerificationCases: A prompt containing shell metacharacters is received verbatim by the fake tool and never interpreted.
A missing tool executable yields TOOL_UNAVAILABLE and no attempt is recorded as ACCEPTED.
A hung tool invocation is killed at timeoutMs and its process tree is no longer alive.
A tool that exits 0 and claims success without editing is not ACCEPTED (NO_CHANGE).
A tool that never fixes the task ends EXHAUSTED after exactly maxAttempts with no PROMOTE.
A tool that commits on its own has its commits folded into exactly one candidate commit.
After any scenario the source repository HEAD, branch list and porcelain status are unchanged.
smoke with an unavailable tool prints SKIPPED and never ACCEPTED.
Any write to packages/core-harness, packages/oracle, packages/agentic-system or docs/blackboard fails scope verification.
The AUTH_FAIL fake exits non-zero without edits; smoke returns SKIPPED TOOL_FAILED_BEFORE_EDIT and never ACCEPTED.
